correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge4k+1\), the first refinement colours precisely the root, its radius-\(k\) neighbourhood and the far tail. Round two distinguishes every individual distance \(j\le2k\) using exact counts \(j\) and \(2k-j+1\). The frontier induction distinguishes each new distance \(j\) by the least previously separated neighbour stratum \(j-k\). Symmetry prevents splitting reflection pairs, and the residual tail coalesces until its final singleton distance, giving precisely \(\lceil(\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1)/k\rceil\) strict rounds. At \(n=4k\), the last two distance strata coincide at round two because the antipodal vertex has two near neighbours; the distinct \(T_{k-1}\) count separates them on round three. Direct and quotient finite programs passed over 869 parameter cases, but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact strict-round count gives a sharp finite-depth bound for 1-dimensional counting refinement on a canonical two-parameter family of symmetric finite structures. The discontinuity at \(n=4k\) arises from a genuine wrap-around neighbour-count collision; composite-order coverage and complete intermediate partitions are beyond the known prime-order eventual partition theorem. These facts quantify information propagation in root-individualized local counting, rather than an arbitrary small numeric gain.
